question: Can a sensitivity-guided variable-length genetic search with per-site coverage and cost attributions find a better coverage-cost trade-off front than a standard variable-length multiobjective GA on a simulated transmitter placement problem?
method: Synthetic transmitter placement; both GAs optimise coverage (train demand) vs cost; fronts are re-evaluated on held-out demand points; hypervolume compared over 3 seeds.

dataset.name: synthetic transmitter placement (400 candidate sites, 1000 demand points, 20x20 grid)

metric_name: test-set hypervolume of normalised coverage-cost front
baseline: Standard variable-length NSGA-II-style GA (add/remove/swap mutation, one-point crossover on site lists); not a verified re-implementation of the paper's operators.
improved: Same GA, population, generations and evaluation budget, plus a population-based site sensitivity (coverage gain per unit cost) that biases add and swap mutations; reports per-site coverage vs cost attributions.
notes: Synthetic instance, so results do not transfer to real deployments. Demand points are split once (75/25) for training and held-out test; test used only for final evaluation. GA settings were fixed a priori, not tuned, so no CV-based selection was needed. Only 3 seeds: std is a rough indication. Dominated fractions are computed on test objectives. Stratification does not apply (no classification labels).
